cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The loop invariants only bound i and end; they say nothing about the contents of nums[0..i]. After the loop Dafny knows only the invariants and !(i <= end), which cannot imply the postcondition that no element before i equals val (e.g. nums[40] = 40 = val is not ruled out). The loop does maintain that property (i only advances past an element that is != val, or after overwriting nums[i] with a non-val nums[end]), so adding the invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> nums[j] != val closes the gap to the postcondition."}
EOF
sed -i 's/^        invariant end < nums.Length$/        invariant end < nums.Length\n        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> nums[j] != val/' program.dfy
sed -n 11,15p program.dfy; dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
Dafny now verifies `program.dfy` with 2 verified and 0 errors.

**What was wrong (an invariant problem, not something to fix in `ensures`):** the loop invariants only gave bounds for `i` and `end`. They said nothing about what the array holds. After the loop, Dafny knows only the invariants plus the exit condition `!(i <= end)`. That isn't enough to prove the postcondition that no element before `i` equals `val`. The counterexample, with `nums[40] = 40 = val`, shows that nothing ruled this out.

**Fix:** I added one loop invariant at line 14:
```dafny
invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> nums[j] != val
```
The loop keeps this true because `i` only moves forward in two cases: when `nums[i] != val` already, or right after `nums[i]` is overwritten with `nums[end]`, which is known not to equal `val`. With this invariant, the exit state implies the postcondition. I didn't change the method body or its contracts.

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before editing. It records `spec_element: "invariant"` and `proof_obligation: "bridge"`.
